source_text: Ἔστι μὲν γὰρ κέντρον τῷ βασιλεῖ, ἀλλ' οὐ χρῆται τούτῳ πρὸς ἄμυναν. Νόμοι τινές εἰσιν οὗτοι τῆς φύσεως ἄγραφοι, ἀργοὺς εἶναι πρὸς τιμωρίαν τοὺς τῶν μεγίστων δυναστειῶν ἐπιβαίνοντας. Ἀλλὰ καὶ ταῖς μελίσσαις, ὅσαι ἂν μὴ ἀκολουθήσωσι τῷ ὑποδείγματι τοῦ βασιλέως, ταχὺ μεταμέλει τῆς ἀβουλίας, ὅτι τῇ πληγῇ τοῦ κέντρου ἐπαποθνήσκουσιν. Ἀκουέτωσαν Χριστιανοὶ, οἷς πρόσταγμά ἐστι μηδενὶ κακὸν ἀντὶ κακοῦ ἀποδιδόναι, ἀλλὰ νικᾶν ἐν τῷ ἀγαθῷ τὸ κακόν. Μίμησαι τῆς μελίσσης τὸ ἰδιότροπον, ὅτι οὐδενὶ λυμαινομένη, οὐδὲ καρπὸν ἀλλότριον διαφθείρουσα, τὰ κηρία συμπήγνυται. Τὸν μὲν γὰρ κηρὸν ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθῶν φανερῶς συναγείρει, τὸ δὲ μέλι, τὴν δροσοειδῶς ἐνεσπαρμένην νοτίδα τοῖς ἄνθεσιν, ἐπισπασαμένη τῷ στόματι, ταύτην ταῖς κοιλότησι τῶν κηρίων ἐνίησιν. Ὅθεν καὶ ὑγρὸν παρὰ τὴν πρώτην ἐστίν· εἶτα τῷ χρόνῳ συμπεφθὲν, πρὸς τὴν οἰκείαν σύ στασιν καὶ ἡδονὴν ἐπανέρχεται. Καλῶν καὶ πρεπόντων αὕτη τῶν ἐπαίνων παρὰ τῆς Παροιμίας τετύχηκε, σοφὴ καὶ ἐργάτις ὀνομασθεῖσα· οὕτω μὲν φιλοπόνως τὴν τροφὴν συναγείρουσα (Ἧς τοὺς πόνους, φησὶ, βασιλεῖς καὶ ἰδιῶται πρὸς ὑγείαν προσφέρονται), οὕτω δὲ σοφῶς φιλοτεχνοῦσα τὰς ἀποθήκας τοῦ μέλιτος (εἰς λεπτὸν γὰρ ὑμένα τὸν κηρὸν διατείνασα, πυκνὰς καὶ συνεχεῖς ἀλλήλαις συνοικοδομεῖ τὰς κοιλότητας), ὡς τὸ πυκνὸν τῆς τῶν μικροτάτων πρὸς ἄλληλα δέσεως, ἔρεισμα γίνεσθαι τῷ παντί. Ἑκάστη γὰρ φρεατία τῆς ἑτέρας ἔχεται, λεπτῷ πρὸς αὐτὴν διειργομένη τε ὁμοῦ καὶ συναπτομένη τῷ διαφράγματι. Ἔπειτα διώροφοι καὶ τριώροφοι αἱ σύριγγες αὗται ἀλλήλαις ἐπῳκοδόμηνται. Ἐφυλάξατο γὰρ μίαν ποιῆσαι διαμπερὲς τὴν κοιλότητα, ἵνα μὴ τῷ βάρει τὸ ὑγρὸν πρὸς τὸ ἐκτὸς διεκπίπτῃ. Κατάμαθε πῶς τὰ τῆς γεωμετρίας εὑρέματα πάρεργά ἐστι τῆς σοφωτάτης μελίσσης. Ἑξάγωνοι γὰρ πᾶσαι καὶ ἰσόπλευροι τῶν κηρίων αἱ σύριγγες, οὐκ ἐπ' εὐθείας ἀλλήλαις κατεπικείμεναι, ἵνα μὴ κάμνωσιν οἱ πυθμένες τοῖς διακένοις ἐφηρμοσμένοι· ἀλλ' αἱ γωνίαι τῶν κάτωθεν ἑξαγώνων, βάθρον καὶ ἔρεισμα τῶν ὑπερκειμένων εἰσὶν, ὡς ἀσφαλῶς ὑπὲρ ἑαυτῶν μετεωρίζειν τὰ βάρη, καὶ ἰδιαζόντως ἑκάστῃ κοιλότητι τὸ ὑγρὸν ἐγκατέχεσθαι. 8.5 Πῶς ἄν σοι πάντα δι' ἀκριβείας ἐπέλθοιμι τὰ ἐν τοῖς βίοις τῶν ὀρνίθων ἰδιώματα; Πῶς μὲν αἱ γέρανοι τὰς ἐν τῇ νυκτὶ προφυλακὰς ἐκ περιτροπῆς ὑποδέχονται· καὶ αἱ μὲν καθεύδουσιν, αἱ δὲ κύκλῳ περιιοῦσαι, πᾶσαν αὐταῖς ἐν τῷ ὕπνῳ παρέχονται τὴν ἀσφάλειαν· εἶτα τοῦ καιροῦ τῆς φυλακῆς πληρουμένου, ἡ μὲν βοήσασα πρὸς ὕπνον ἐτράπετο, ἡ δὲ τὴν διαδοχὴν ὑποδεξαμένη, ἧς ἔτυχεν ἀσφαλείας ἀντέδωκεν ἐν τῷ μέρει. Ταύτην καὶ ἐν τῇ πτήσει τὴν εὐταξίαν κατόψει. Ἄλλοτε γὰρ ἄλλη τὴν ὁδηγίαν ἐκδέχεται, καὶ τακτόν τινα χρόνον προκαθηγησαμένη τῆς πτήσεως, εἰς τὸ κατόπιν περιελθοῦσα, τῇ μεθ' ἑαυτὴν τὴν ἡγεμονίαν τῆς ὁδοῦ παραδίδωσι. Τὸ δὲ τῶν πελαργῶν οὐδὲ πόρρω ἐστὶ συνέσεως λογικῆς· οὕτω μὲν κατὰ τὸν ἕνα καιρὸν πάντας ἐπιδημεῖν τοῖς τῇδε χωρίοις· οὕτω δὲ ὑφ' ἑνὶ συνθήματι πάντας ἀπαίρειν. Δορυφοροῦσι δὲ αὐτοὺς αἱ παρ' ἡμῖν κορῶναι, καὶ παραπέμπουσιν, ἐμοὶ δοκεῖν, καὶ συμμαχίαν τινὰ παρεχόμεναι πρὸς ὄρνιθας πολεμίους. Σημεῖον δὲ, πρῶτον μὲν τὸ μὴ φαίνεσθαι ὑπὸ τὸν καιρὸν ἐκεῖνον κορώνην παντάπασιν, ἔπειθ' ὅτι μετὰ τραυμάτων ἐπανερχόμεναι ἐναργῆ τοῦ συνασπισμοῦ καὶ τῆς ἐπιμαχίας τὰ σημεῖα κομίζουσι.
thought_title: The bee's sting, honeycomb geometry, and the order of cranes and storks
orientation: Basil is continuing his survey of the natural world, now describing the bee's restraint and craftsmanship, then turning to the orderly behavior of cranes and storks as moral examples for Christians.
pass_a_gloss: For the king has a sting, but he does not use it for defense. These are certain unwritten laws of nature, that those who mount the greatest powers are slow to punish. But also for the bees, as many as do not follow the example of the king, quickly regret their folly, because they die upon the blow of the sting. Let Christians hear, for whom it is a command to repay no one evil for evil, but to overcome evil with good. Imitate the peculiar character of the bee, that she, harming no one, nor destroying another's fruit, builds her combs together. For she gathers the wax openly from the flowers, and the honey, the dew-like moisture scattered in the flowers, drawing it up with her mouth, she pours this into the hollows of the combs. Whence also it is liquid at first; then, ripened by time, it returns to its own consistency and sweetness. She has obtained beautiful and fitting praises from the Proverb, being called wise and a worker; so industriously gathering her food (whose labors, it says, kings and private persons bring forward for health), and so wisely crafting the storehouses of the honey (for stretching the wax into a thin membrane, she builds together the hollows dense and continuous with one another), so that the density of the binding of the smallest parts to one another becomes a support for the whole. For each little cell holds to the other, being at once separated from it by a thin partition and joined to it by the dividing wall. Then these tubes are built upon one another two-storied and three-storied. For she guarded against making one hollow through and through, lest by its weight the liquid should escape to the outside. Learn how the discoveries of geometry are the by-work of the most wise bee. For all the tubes of the combs are hexagonal and equal-sided, not lying upon one another in straight lines, lest the bottoms should be strained, fitted upon empty spaces; but the angles of the hexagons below are a base and support of those above, so as safely to hold up the weights above themselves, and particularly for the liquid to be contained in each hollow. 8.5 How could I go through for you with precision all the peculiarities in the lives of birds? How the cranes receive the night watches in turn; and some sleep, while others going around in a circle provide all safety for them in their sleep; then when the time of the watch is fulfilled, the one having cried out turns to sleep, and the one having received the succession gives back in turn the safety which she happened to receive. You will see this good order also in their flight. For at different times a different one receives the guidance, and having led the flight for a fixed time, going around to the rear, she hands over the leadership of the way to the one after herself. The behavior of the storks is not far from rational understanding; so at one season all arrive in the regions here; so at one signal all depart. The crows among us escort them and send them on their way, it seems to me, providing also some alliance against hostile birds. And the sign is, first, that no crow appears at all at that season, then that returning with wounds they bring clear signs of the fighting together and the battle-aid.

choices.term: ἀργοὺς εἶναι πρὸς τιμωρίαν τοὺς τῶν μεγίστων δυναστειῶν ἐπιβαίνοντας
choices.english: that those who mount the greatest powers are slow to punish
choices.why: Keeps the literal force of 'mounting' (ἐπιβαίνοντας) as ascending to power, and 'slow' (ἀργοὺς) as inactive or sluggish toward punishment, preserving the paradox Basil draws between power and restraint.
rejected: that those who hold the greatest powers are reluctant to punish
that those who attain the greatest powers are idle in punishment

choices.english: they die upon the blow of the sting
choices.why: The compound ἐπαποθνῄσκουσιν means dying as a direct result of the blow; 'upon the blow' preserves the causal immediacy and the literal sense of the preposition.
rejected: they die from the sting's blow
they perish by the sting's stroke

choices.why: ἰδιότροπον means a distinctive or peculiar way of being; 'peculiar character' captures the sense of a unique nature or disposition without importing modern moral overtones.

choices.english: the dew-like moisture scattered in the flowers
choices.why: The adverb δροσοειδῶς modifies how the moisture is scattered; keeping 'dew-like' as an adverb of manner preserves the image of moisture distributed like dew.

choices.english: are the by-work of the most wise bee
choices.why: πάρεργα means secondary or incidental work; 'by-work' preserves the sense that geometry is a side product of the bee's activity, not its primary aim.
rejected: are the incidental products of the most wise bee
are the side-effects of the most wise bee

choices.why: περιτροπή means rotation or succession; 'in turn' captures the alternating, rotating nature of the watch without over-translating.

bible_refs.note: νικᾶν ἐν τῷ ἀγαθῷ τὸ κακόν
σοφὴ καὶ ἐργάτις ὀνομασθεῖσα; Basil cites the LXX description of the bee as wise and a worker

pass_b_english: The king does have a sting, but he does not use it for self-defense. These are unwritten laws of nature: that those who mount the greatest powers are slow to punish. And among the bees, any that do not follow the example of the king quickly regret their folly, because they die upon the blow of the sting. Let Christians hear this—Christians who have the command to repay no one evil for evil, but to overcome evil with good (Romans 12:17, 21). Imitate the peculiar character of the bee: it harms no one, it destroys no one else's fruit, and yet it builds its combs. For it gathers the wax openly from the flowers, and the honey—the dew-like moisture scattered in the flowers—it draws in with its mouth and pours into the hollows of the combs. At first the honey is liquid; then, ripened by time, it returns to its own proper consistency and sweetness. This bee has received fine and fitting praise from Proverbs, where it is called wise and a worker (Proverbs 6:8)—so industriously does it gather its food (whose labors, it says, kings and common people alike consume for their health), and so wisely does it craft its storehouses of honey. For it stretches the wax into a thin membrane and builds the hollows close together and continuous with one another, so that the density of the tiny cells bound to each other becomes a support for the whole. Each little cell holds to the next, separated from it by a thin dividing wall and at the same time joined to it. Then these tubes are built upon one another in two and three stories. The bee has been careful not to make one hollow running straight through, so that the liquid does not escape to the outside under its own weight. Learn how the discoveries of geometry are the by-work of the most wise bee. All the tubes of the combs are hexagonal and equal-sided, and they do not lie directly on top of one another, so that the bottoms do not suffer strain when fitted onto empty gaps. Rather, the angles of the hexagons below serve as a base and support for those above, so that they safely hold up the weights above them, and the liquid is contained separately in each hollow.

How could I go through for you in detail all the distinctive traits in the lives of birds? How the cranes take up the night watches in turn: some sleep, while others circle around and provide them with complete safety in their sleep; then, when the time of the watch is fulfilled, the one that has called out turns to sleep, and the one that takes over the succession gives back in turn the safety it received. You will see this same good order in their flight. For at different times a different crane takes up the lead, and after guiding the flight for a fixed time, it moves to the rear and hands over the leadership of the way to the one behind it. The behavior of the storks is not far from rational understanding: they all arrive in these regions at one and the same season, and they all depart at one and the same signal. Our crows escort them and accompany them, providing, it seems to me, a kind of alliance against hostile birds. The proof is, first, that no crow appears at all during that season, and second, that when they return with wounds, they carry clear signs of the battle fought and the defense given.

problems.quote: so that the bottoms do not weaken by being fitted onto empty spaces
problems.source_quote: ἵνα μὴ κάμνωσιν οἱ πυθμένες τοῖς διακένοις ἐφηρμοσμένοι
problems.why: διακενῶν means 'gaps/empty spaces'; the point is bottoms aren't fitted onto gaps, not that they weaken.
problems.fix: so that the bottoms are not fitted onto empty gaps
problems.ruling: κάμνωσιν means 'weary/grow tired,' not 'weaken'; διακένοις means 'empty/gaps.' The point is bottoms aren't fitted onto gaps, not that they weaken from being so fitted.

problems.quote: bring to their tables for health
problems.source_quote: βασιλεῖς καὶ ἰδιῶται πρὸς ὑγείαν προσφέρονται
problems.why: Missing 'kings and common people' as subjects; the English makes 'whose labors' the object, but 'prosferontai' means they bring/consume it, not that they bring the labors.
problems.fix: whose labors, it says, kings and common people consume for their health
problems.ruling: 'βασιλεῖς καὶ ἰδιῶται' are subjects of 'προσφέρονται'; English omits them, losing 'kings and common people' as agents.

edits.old: so that the bottoms do not weaken by being fitted onto empty spaces
edits.new: so that the bottoms are not fitted onto empty gaps

edits.old: whose labors, Scripture says, kings and common people alike bring to their tables for health
edits.new: whose labors, Scripture says, kings and common people alike consume for their health

fixed: Corrected 'do not weaken by being fitted onto empty spaces' to 'are not fitted onto empty gaps' to match the source's point about the bottoms not resting on gaps.
Corrected 'bring to their tables for health' to 'consume for their health' to reflect that kings and common people consume the honey, not the labors.

problems.why: In the bee context, βασιλεύς refers to the queen bee (in ancient Greek, bees have 'kings,' not knowing queen bees are female). The English keeps 'king' which is historically accurate to the source. Not an error per glossary. However, the first sentence 'The king does have a sting'—actually queen bees DO have stings, and worker bees too. Drone bees (males) do not. The ancient belief was that the 'king' bee didn't sting. The English correctly preserves this. Not an error.

The Greek φησὶ refers to the proverb about kings and common people consuming the bee's labors for health. The English inserts 'Scripture says' which is not in the Greek—φησὶ is a simple 'says' without specifying the speaker. This makes it seem like a scriptural citation when it's part of the proverbial saying about the bee, not a biblical quote marker.
problems.fix: so industriously does it gather its food (whose labors, it says, kings and common people alike consume for their health)
problems.ruling: φησὶ is bare 'says'; 'Scripture says' wrongly implies a biblical citation for a non-scriptural proverb.

problems.quote: the bottoms are not fitted onto empty gaps
problems.source_quote: ἵνα μὴ κάμνωσιν οἱ πυθμένες τοῖς διακένοις ἐφηρμοσμένοι
problems.why: κάμνωσιν means 'suffer' or 'be distressed/weakened,' not 'fitted.' The sense is 'so that the bottoms do not suffer by being fitted onto empty gaps' or 'so that the bottoms are not strained/unsupported when fitted onto gaps.' 'Are not fitted' changes the meaning—the bottoms ARE fitted, but they don't suffer from it due to the hexagonal arrangement.
problems.fix: so that the bottoms do not suffer strain when fitted onto empty gaps
problems.ruling: κάμνωσιν means 'suffer/strain'; 'are not fitted' mistranslates, losing the sense that bottoms would suffer if on gaps.

edits.old: Scripture says, kings and common people alike consume for their health
edits.new: it says, kings and common people alike consume for their health

edits.old: so that the bottoms are not fitted onto empty gaps
edits.new: so that the bottoms do not suffer strain when fitted onto empty gaps

fixed: No fix needed: 'the king' correctly preserves the ancient Greek belief that the bee ruler (βασιλεύς) has a sting but does not use it; the source says 'κέντρον τῷ βασιλεῖ' and the English accurately renders this.
Fixed: 'Scripture says' inserted a speaker not in the Greek; φησὶ is a simple 'it says' referring to the proverbial saying, so removed 'Scripture'.
Fixed: 'are not fitted' misread κάμνωσιν; the Greek means the bottoms do not suffer or strain when fitted onto empty gaps, so changed to 'do not suffer strain when fitted onto empty gaps'.

last_rejected.quote: it draws in with its mouth and pours into the hollows
last_rejected.source_quote: ἐπισπασαμένη τῷ στόματι, ταύτην ταῖς κοιλότησι τῶν κηρίων ἐνίησιν
last_rejected.why: ἐπισπασαμένη means 'having drawn in/aspirated,' but the key issue is ἐνίησιν which means 'puts into' or 'inserts,' not 'pours into.' The bee doesn't pour liquid honey; it deposits the moisture into the cells. 'Pours' suggests a different action.
last_rejected.fix: it draws in with its mouth and deposits it in the hollows
last_rejected.ruling: ἐνίησιν can mean 'pours into'; LSJ cites this passage. Normal range for liquid deposited into cells.
